steps.title: Open the Desk page
steps.narration: The Desk page scans about 100 well-known stocks. It ranks each one by how close it sits to a key price level, and names the exact price bar behind that measurement.
steps.point_out: Today's ranked list. Each row names the exact price bar its distance was measured from.

steps.title: See the Desk before any top-up has run
steps.narration: Refreshing the Desk's price data is called a "top-up." Before the first one is recorded, the Top-up Runs panel says so in plain words — "No top-up runs recorded yet." — with no rows and no stand-in numbers.
steps.point_out: The Top-up Runs panel at the foot of the page: zero rows, and one sentence stating that nothing has been recorded yet.

capture.note: Static frame, spliced in by the iteration-13 audit. This state is a one-way door: it was captured on THIS rig's live, already-booted /desk page at 2026-07-28T17:02Z, before the first of the three checkpoint runs was written at 17:03:23Z, so a live re-record on the same (now-populated) rig can never reproduce it. Re-running demo_runner.py --mode record against this script would overwrite step-02.png with a populated frame.

steps.title: See every top-up run saved for good
steps.narration: After three runs were recorded on that same Desk, the panel lists all three — one ordinary run, one cancelled part-way through, and one that hit a problem. Each result is saved for good, and a later run is added beside the earlier ones, never on top of them.
steps.point_out: Three recorded runs: two that ran to the end and one cancelled after 3 of 404 pairs — each row showing its own real recorded state, not a placeholder.

steps.title: See exactly how each run went
steps.narration: Every run's outcome is broken down clearly: how many pairs were checked, how many succeeded, and how many hit a problem.
steps.point_out: This run finished all 404 pairs attempted, with 403 fetched and 1 that could not be fetched.

steps.title: See the exact reason a pair failed
steps.narration: When a top-up run hits a real problem, the Desk shows the exact reason. It never hides behind a vague error message.
steps.point_out: One pair could not be fetched. The real, specific reason is spelled out in full.

expect.text: AAPL 1h — no data for that window

steps.title: Look back at a past scan
steps.narration: Every past scan is saved. Opening one shows it exactly as it was recorded, never mixed with today's numbers.
steps.point_out: A note confirms this is an older, saved scan, not today's.

expect.text: Viewing the recorded screen for 2026-06-22 — not the latest.

steps.title: Jump from a ranked stock into its chart
steps.narration: Clicking any ranked stock opens that stock's own chart, already loaded for the same date.
steps.point_out: The Structure page opens with AAPL's own chart and price-level table, both loaded for that date.

steps.title: Move to the live tape reader
steps.narration: The Desk sits alongside two other pages, all reachable from the same menu at the top.
steps.point_out: The Cockpit page opens, ready to watch a stock's price action.

steps.title: Choose the simulated tape
steps.narration: You can try the reader on a made-up stock first. No live market feed is needed.
steps.point_out: The Simulated option is now selected.

steps.title: Name the simulated ticker
steps.narration: Typing a name sets up which made-up stock the tape will follow.
steps.point_out: The ticker field now holds the name just typed.

steps.title: Watch the tape settle into a read
steps.narration: Price bars move in real time. The tape settles into a plain-English read, like "Buyer Control."
steps.point_out: The live read label sits just above the moving price bars.

steps.title: Open the price-level map fresh
steps.narration: The Structure page maps a stock's key support and resistance levels. This time, the symbol and date are typed in by hand.
steps.point_out: An empty form, waiting for a stock symbol and a date.

steps.title: Choose a stock to map
steps.narration: Typing in a stock loads its own price levels.
steps.point_out: The Symbol field now reads AAPL.

steps.title: Choose the date to look at
steps.narration: Typing in the exact date and time to look at.
steps.point_out: The As-of field now reads the chosen date and time.

steps.title: Load its key price levels
steps.narration: Loading draws the stock's real price history, with its key support and resistance levels marked on top.
steps.point_out: The chart and the level table both show a level near 300.11 — a well-known price wall for this stock.
